comments.note: In scripts/cli.js cmdPublishSkills(), CLI args (e.g. --dry-run) are forwarded to build-skills.js but not to publish-skills.js. This means 'node scripts/cli.js publish-skills --dry-run' builds in check mode but still writes published files. Consider forwarding args to publish-skills.js as well if it supports dry-run semantics, or document the asymmetry.

The Skills menu items use category 'Skills' rather than 'Personas' as suggested in WP notes. This is actually better UX — Skills are a distinct concept — but the WP notes and the actual implementation diverge. The implementation choice is correct.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified independently via live execution.
AC #1: `node scripts/cli.js build-skills` delegates correctly to build-skills.js; exit code propagates via process.exit(code). Verified with --check and --strict flags.
AC #2: `node scripts/cli.js publish-skills` invokes build-skills.js first, then publish-skills.js. Abort-on-failure guard confirmed in source (buildCode !== 0 → process.exit). Sequencing correct.
AC #3: `node scripts/cli.js help` shows both `build-skills` and `publish-skills` under the 'Skills' category section.
AC #4: AGENTS.md Root-Level Tooling table contains full entries for both scripts/build-skills.js and scripts/publish-skills.js (lines 364–365).
AC #5: docs/references/menu-guide.md has both commands in a dedicated '### Skills' section (table rows) and in the CLI examples block.
Regression: 84/84 workspace tests pass; 3353/3353 MCP server tests pass. No regressions.
Edge cases: unknown flags silently ignored (graceful); exit code guard prevents publish when build fails; --dry-run only applies to build step (known low-priority asymmetry).

comments.note: In cmdPublishSkills() (scripts/cli.js:405), CLI args (e.g. --dry-run) are forwarded to build-skills.js but NOT to publish-skills.js. Passing --dry-run results in build running in check mode (no dist/ output) while publish-skills.js still writes files. This is a UX inconsistency but not a functional bug — no AC requires symmetric dry-run behavior. Previously flagged by Developer; confirmed here.
No automated test covers the build→publish sequencing or the abort-on-build-fail guard in cmdPublishSkills. A unit test mocking runScript() would catch regression if the call order is ever changed.
